sections.label: Age discrimination and economy
sections.summary: Age discrimination can reduce the economy's overall competitiveness and productivity, beyond affecting individual workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Tan (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: Beyond affecting individual workers, age discrimination can reduce our economy's overall competitiveness and productivity.

sections.label: Workplace Fairness Act and dispute resolution
sections.summary: The Workplace Fairness Act prohibits workplace discrimination based on protected characteristics including age, and the Workplace Fairness (Dispute Resolution) Bill sets out the claims process.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Tan (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: These cases show how age discrimination, if unaddressed, can lead to costly legal battles and a fractured workplace culture.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Tan (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: This is why the Workplace Fairness Act (WFA) is an important step that prohibits workplace discrimination based on protected characteristics, including age.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Tan (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: Today, I welcome the introduction of the Workplace Fairness (Dispute Resolution) Bill, which sets out the process for individuals to make claims against firms if they experience workplace discrimination.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Tan (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: These are timely measures as Singapore is expected to become a super-aged society in 2026.

sections.label: Union mediation compensation outcome
sections.summary: Through union mediation, he secured approximately $55,000 in compensation more than if he had escalated to the Employment Claims Tribunal.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Tan (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: Through union mediation, he secured approximately $55,000 in compensation more than if he had escalated to the Employment Claims Tribunal (ECT).

sections.label: AI recruitment discrimination lawsuit
sections.summary: Workday, Inc. faces a collective action lawsuit claiming its AI-powered recruitment system discriminated against candidates above 40 years old, prompting NTUC to ask for stronger AI governance standards.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Tan (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: In the United States, for instance, Workday, Inc., one of the world's largest HR software provider, is facing a collective action lawsuit based on claims that its AI-powered recruitment system discriminated against candidates above 40 years old.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Tan (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: This shows that even well-established platforms are not immune to bias and that algorithm discrimination is a real and emerging risk.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Tan (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: So, NTUC asks for stronger guidance and governance standards for AI-powered HR systems to ensure that technology promotes fairness, not perpetuate hidden discrimination.

sections.label: Expanding ECT claims limit
sections.summary: NTUC asks the Ministry to consider expanding the ECT claims limit for other workplace claims beyond workplace discrimination, including salary dispute and unfair dismissal.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Tan (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: Given the advantages of ECT in granting more workers, including our PMEs, access to justice, we ask that the Ministry do consider expanding the ECT claims limit for other workplace claims beyond workplace discrimination, including salary dispute and unfair dismissal.

sections.label: Senior workers in super-aged society
sections.summary: Singapore will enter a super-aged society in 2026, and senior workers often face anxieties regarding job security, re-employment and skills retraining.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Tan (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: Singapore will enter a super-aged society in 2026, and our senior workers often face anxieties regarding job security, re-employment and skills retraining.

sections.label: Disability awareness training for dispute staff
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether HR professionals, TADM mediators, ECT staff and High Court personnel in employment disputes can undergo mandatory disability awareness training.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The sensory environment of the meetings, the bright fluorescent lights, the hum of the air-conditioning and the unpredictability of the discussion, left him feeling psychologically unsafe and unable to articulate his case clearly.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: This is why my first and most urgent clarification is this: is it possible for HR professionals, TADM mediators, ECT staff and High Court personnel involved in employment disputes, to undergo mandatory disability awareness training.

sections.label: Representation by social service agencies
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether the Bill can allow social service agencies or non-profit organisations to represent persons with disabilities in mediation and tribunal proceedings.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: In turn, parties may be represented by advocates and solicitors if claims exceed certain thresholds.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: But Sir, is there space for the provisions under the Bill to go further by allowing social service agencies or non-profit organisations working with such groups of people to represent persons with disabilities during mediation sessions and tribunal proceedings?

sections.label: WCAG compliance for dispute materials
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether all materials, guidelines and submission portals for workplace fairness disputes can comply with the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Would it be possible to ensure that all materials, guidelines and submission portals related to workplace fairness disputes comply with the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG).

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: They are already mandatory for high-traffic Government websites under our Digital Service Standards, with full compliance expected by 2030.

sections.label: Accessible and fair dispute system
sections.summary: The speaker supports the Bill and calls for disability awareness training, disability organisation representation and accessible systems so persons with disabilities are treated with dignity.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The Workplace Fairness (Dispute Resolution) Bill is a commendable, intentional and balanced step to building a system that truly serves everyone.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: I am deeply grateful to the Minister and the entire Ministry team for their dedication in crafting this landmark piece of legislation, and call on all of us to deliberately and intentionally ensure that the provisions made in this Bill continue to build a system that is accessible and fair for all workers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: When we train our mediators and tribunal officers in disability awareness, we ensure that persons with disabilities are treated with dignity and understanding.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: When we enable disability organisations to represent persons with disabilities, we level the playing field and ensure that power imbalances do not predetermine outcomes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: When we make our systems accessible – our portals, forms, hearing rooms – we remove barriers that exclude persons with disabilities from seeking justice.

sections.label: Support for Workplace Fairness Bill
sections.summary: The speaker supports the Bill as aligning Singapore's labour legislation with global peers, providing clarity for companies and signalling that discrimination is not tolerated.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: It is now far harder to strike a balance between the needs and interests of employers and employees, especially for a small country with a globally-connected economy like Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I am standing in support of this Bill because it is an important Bill that aligns Singapore's labour legislation with that of global peers and provides much-needed clarity for companies that choose to operate here.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The Bill sends an important message: that discrimination has never been and will never be tolerated in our workplaces.

sections.label: Mediation-first dispute resolution approach
sections.summary: The mediation-first approach lets disputes be resolved less adversarially and allows some semblance of relationship to be preserved.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The mediation-first approach means that disputes can be resolved in a less adversarial manner and allows for the possibility that some semblance of relationship can be preserved.

sections.label: Monitoring the regime in practice
sections.summary: The speaker hopes the Government devotes resources to monitor how the regime works in practice, including time, cost, outcomes and objectives.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Fourth, I hope that the Government devotes some resources to monitor how the entire regime works in practice: examining the average time to resolution, cost to parties, outcomes and whether the mediation-first approach is achieving the harmony and fairness objectives intended.

sections.label: Mandatory mediation before adjudication
sections.summary: The Bill introduces mandatory mediation before adjudication.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: First, this Bill introduces mandatory mediation before adjudication.

sections.label: Accessible and impartial mediation
sections.summary: The speaker asks how mediation will be ensured to be not just available but also accessible and impartial, especially for lower-wage workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: How will we ensure that mediation is not just available, but also accessible and impartial, especially for our lower-wage workers?

sections.label: Safeguards and training for employees
sections.summary: The speaker asks what safeguards and training will be in place so employees can resolve grievances without fear or duress.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Could the Ministry share what safeguards and training will be in place to ensure employees can resolve grievances without fear or duress?

sections.label: How compensation will be determined
sections.summary: The speaker asks how compensation will be determined and whether guidelines similar to those at the ECT will apply.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: To clarify, can the Minister share how compensation will be determined and whether guidelines, similar to those at the ECT, will apply?

sections.label: Statutory framework for workplace fairness
sections.summary: The Bill marks a landmark first for Singapore: a comprehensive, statutory framework for workplace fairness and anti-discrimination.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The Bill marks a landmark first for Singapore – the establishment of a comprehensive, statutory framework for workplace fairness and anti-discrimination.

sections.label: Statutory anti-discrimination protections for employees
sections.summary: This Bill stands between the first part of the WFA passed in January and statutory anti-discrimination protections employees can use.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: After we passed the first part of the WFA in January this year, this Bill now stands between us and finally having statutory anti-discrimination protections that employees can avail themselves of.

sections.label: Mediation request deadlines
sections.summary: New section 36E requires a mediation request within one, two or six months of the alleged discriminatory employment decision, depending on the claim and notice.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The new section 36E to be introduced by this Bill, provides that a mediation request must be made within one, two or six months of the alleged discriminatory employment decision, depending on the nature of the claim and whether the employer gave notice of the employment decision or not.

sections.label: Discriminatory hiring claim notice provisions
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether section 36E(2)(b) is meaningful given express provisions on deemed and implied notice where a prospective employer ghosted the employee.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Where a claim for a discriminatory hiring decision is concerned, is section 36E(2)(b) even meaningful since there are express provisions on deemed notice and implied notice where a prospective employer has "ghosted" the employee after the employment application, interview or test?

sections.label: Workplace fairness claims court and tribunal
sections.summary: Unresolved workplace fairness claims may go to the General Division of the High Court or the ECT if the claim is S$250,000 or less, with no lawyers in the ECT.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: At the third and final stage, any workplace fairness claims that cannot be resolved through the company's internal processes or through mediation may be brought to the General Division of the High Court, or to the Employment Claims Tribunal (ECT) if the claim amount is S$250,000 or less.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: For cases brought to the ECT, individuals are not permitted to be represented by lawyers, whether during mediation or during tribunal proceedings.

sections.label: Remedies for workplace fairness claims
sections.summary: Clause 36N and section 12A stipulate remedies: damages generally, and for discriminatory dismissal claims an additional option of reinstatement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: That seems complicated and confusing for an individual to navigate without a lawyer.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: And in terms of remedies, Mr Speaker, the new clause 36N to be introduced in the WFA, as well as the new section 12A to be introduced in the Employment Claims Act 2016, stipulate the remedies that an individual can obtain in a WFA claim.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: In essence, the general relief that the claimant can obtain is damages and for discriminatory dismissal claims, there is an additional option of ordering reinstatement of the claimant in his or her previous employment.

sections.label: Educating workers on calculating claimed losses
sections.summary: The speaker suggests publishing illustrations and infographics on calculating claimed losses and asks if WFA decisions will be consolidated publicly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Three, we can publish simple illustrations and infographics to educate workers on how to calculate their claimed losses, all centralised in one accessible location.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Would the Ministry publish and consolidate WFA decisions on a publicly accessible website, as done by the Personal Data Protection Commission?

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: This would help employees understand how damages have been assessed and serve the goals of deterrence and open justice as errant employers are named and taken to task.

sections.label: Support for the Bill
sections.summary: The speaker fully supports the Bill despite the clarifications sought.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Notwithstanding the clarifications sought, I fully support the Bill, Mr Speaker.

sections.label: Three-step discrimination grievance framework
sections.summary: The Bill introduces a three-step framework for discrimination grievances, consistent with Singapore's tripartite model of trust and shared responsibility.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: It is often better for both worker and employer to resolve disputes early through open communication, internal processes and mediation rather than escalation and litigation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: This Bill, therefore, introduces a three-step framework for handling discrimination grievances and this staged approach is consistent with Singapore's long-standing tripartite model: one built on trust, mutual respect and the shared responsibility between the Government, employers and workers.

sections.label: Protection for smaller companies
sections.summary: The speaker seeks clarification on how workers in companies with fewer than 25 employees will be protected.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: Thirdly, I note that the Workplace Fairness Legislation currently applies to employers with more than 25 employees.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: While this covers the majority of workers, about close to 18% of companies in Singapore employ fewer than 25 people.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: These are often the most vulnerable workplaces where HR structures are informal and power dynamics can be more pronounced.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: I, therefore, seek clarification on how workers in these smaller companies will be protected.

sections.label: Workplace discrimination remains a concern
sections.summary: Although the situation has improved significantly, workplace discrimination remains a concern for many Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: Although the situation today has changed and improved significantly, workplace discrimination remains a concern for many Singaporeans.

sections.label: Dispute Resolution Bill and early resolution
sections.summary: The Dispute Resolution Bill shows commitment to fair treatment, but most disputes should be resolved early through internal processes and joint discussions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: Together with the Dispute Resolution Bill presented today, it demonstrates our nation's commitment to ensuring every worker is treated fairly, respected and given equal opportunities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: However, for the legislation to be truly effective, most disputes should be resolved at an early stage — through internal grievance processes and joint discussions.

sections.label: Fair treatment and equal opportunities
sections.summary: They affirm that every worker, regardless of protected characteristics, deserves fair treatment and equal opportunities to thrive.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: They show that while we value competitiveness and meritocracy, we also value compassion and justice.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: They affirm that every worker regardless of race, gender, age, religion, disability, family status or any of the protected characteristics deserves to be treated fairly and have equal opportunities to thrive.

sections.label: Workplace discrimination enforcement approach
sections.summary: The WFA provides for both private claims and state enforcement, each serving different purposes.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Mr Saktiandi Supaat asked whether this Bill signals the Government's intent for workplace discrimination to be addressed through private claims rather than state enforcement.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: This is not the case – the WFA provides for both and each serves different purposes.

sections.label: WFA baseline grievance requirements
sections.summary: The WFA will set baseline requirements such as requiring employers to have a written grievance handling process.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: The WFA will set baseline requirements such as requiring employers to have a written grievance handling process in place.

sections.label: Bill prohibits employer retaliation
sections.summary: The first Bill prohibits employers from retaliating against those who raised a workplace grievance, including by cancelling work passes.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: The first Bill prohibits employers from retaliating against those who have raised a workplace grievance, including by cancelling their work passes.

sections.label: Claim filing duration
sections.summary: The duration to file court claims will be prescribed in subsidiary legislation, referencing four weeks from claim referral certificate issuance.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Mr Saktiandi asked about the duration claimants would have to file their claims to the courts when the dispute cannot be resolved by mediation.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: This duration will be prescribed in subsidiary legislation, referencing the current duration of four weeks from the issuance of the claim referral certificate for other ECT claims.

sections.label: ECT threshold for discrimination claims
sections.summary: The ECT's threshold has been expanded to $250,000 for workplace discrimination claims, allowing more PMEs to file claims.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: As we have expanded the ECT's threshold to $250,000 for workplace discrimination claims, this means that even more PMEs can file claims.

sections.label: Union representation and tripartism
sections.summary: Allowing unions to represent workers not recognised by employers would undermine tripartism and seed adversarial union-employer relations.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Allowing unions to represent workers when they have not been recognised by their employer would undermine this fundamental tenet of tripartism and seed an adversarial relationship between unions and employers, to the detriment of industrial peace and workplace harmony in Singapore.

sections.label: Claim limits and damages
sections.summary: Clause 14 gives MOM discretion to set claim limits for all workplace discrimination claims in the ECT, and the Bill does not prescribe new heads of claim such as injury to feelings.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: To clarify, clause 14 of the Bill actually provides MOM with the discretion to set claim limits for all types of workplace discrimination claims in the ECT, including for in- and end-employment claims.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: To Mr Dennis Tan's question on whether this Bill introduces new heads of claim for damages, such as injury to feelings, emotions, this is not prescribed in the Bill.

sections.label: Public access to WFA judgments
sections.summary: Making WFA judgments publicly accessible will help employers and workers understand how the law is applied, and the courts are being worked with on this.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Making WFA judgments publicly accessible will help employers and workers better understand how the law is applied.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: We are working with the courts on making ECT judgments publicly accessible and this will include WFA judgments.

sections.label: Bill timeline and purpose
sections.summary: The Bill aims to strengthen protections for jobseekers and employees against workplace discrimination, with work towards a timeline of end-2027.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Members of the House, let us focus on this Bill, which is to strengthen protections for jobseekers and employees against workplace discrimination.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: We are working towards the timeline of end-2027 because we recognise the significant scale of the work that lies ahead.

sections.label: Exemption for small firms
sections.summary: Small firms with fewer than 25 employees are exempt for a start, with tripartite partners and TAFEP to ramp up their capabilities, and the exemption reviewed five years after implementation.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: As mentioned, when moving the Workplace Fairness Bill in January, small firms may not have the resources or expertise to comprehensively implement the new rules.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Hence, we decided to exempt small firms with fewer than 25 employees for a start, and we will work with tripartite partners and TAFEP to ramp up the capabilities of these firms.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: This exemption will be reviewed five years after the law is implemented.

sections.label: Thanks to stakeholders and Members
sections.summary: The speaker thanks stakeholders including employers, HR professionals, non-governmental organisations, legal practitioners and the public, and Members past and current for suggestions raised.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: I also want to thank the various stakeholders who took the time and the effort to contribute to our engagements, including the employers, our HR professionals, our non-governmental organisations, the legal practitioners and members of the public.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: I want to thank Members, both from the past, in January, the past term of Government to the current term of Government, for the suggestions raised, and many of which are also ongoing in discussions still with tripartite partners.

sections.label: Efforts before WFA commencement
sections.summary: Efforts already underway will continue after the Bill is passed so that when the WFA comes into force at end-2027, employers understand their duties and workers know their rights.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: As I shared earlier, efforts are already underway.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: These will continue once the Bill is passed so that when the WFA comes into force at the end of 2027, employers will fully understand their duties and workers will clearly know their rights.

sections.label: Workplace Fairness Act protections
sections.summary: The Workplace Fairness Act strengthens protections for jobseekers and employees against workplace discrimination, complementing the Tripartite Guidelines on Fair Employment Practices.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Adil saksama asas harmoni, Tempat kerja makmur dan berseri." Just as the cempaka flower flourishes with the morning dew, a workplace thrives when fairness and equality are upheld.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Justice ensures trust and respect, nurturing harmony and productivity amongst all employees.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: The new Workplace Fairness Act (WFA) is a landmark legislation that strengthens protections for jobseekers and employees against workplace discrimination.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: It complements the existing Tripartite Guidelines on Fair Employment Practices (TGFEP), by: First, prohibiting employers from making adverse employment decisions based on protected characteristics.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: These are: nationality; age; sex, marital status, pregnancy, caregiving responsibilities; race, religion and language ability; and disability and mental health conditions.

sections.label: Mediation before adjudication requirement
sections.summary: Section 36D requires claimants to attempt mediation before bringing a claim to adjudication in the Court.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: The new section 36D of the Act sets out the requirement that claimants must attempt mediation before they can bring a claim to adjudication in the Court.

sections.label: Mediator training and service providers
sections.summary: Mediators receive customised training, and providers like the Singapore Mediation Centre will mediate higher value claims above $30,000 with more stringent mediator requirements.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: This includes customised training programmes to equip them with varied mediation approaches to deal with complex workplace discrimination disputes; and coverage of inclusivity and sensitivity training to better serve a range of individuals, including persons with disabilities and persons with mental health conditions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: We will also appoint other mediation service providers such as the Singapore Mediation Centre to mediate higher value claims above $30,000.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: We will set more stringent requirements on mediators for higher value claims, including possessing legal qualifications or having relevant experience mediating employment disputes.

sections.label: Expanded ECT jurisdiction
sections.summary: The ECT's jurisdiction will be expanded to hear workplace discrimination claims up to and including $250,000.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: To make the ECT's affordable and expeditious adjudication process accessible to more workers, we will expand the ECT's jurisdiction to hear workplace discrimination claims up to and including $250,000.

sections.label: Higher claims limit scope
sections.summary: The higher claims limit applies only to workplace fairness disputes, not salary-related claims or wrongful dismissal.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: The higher claims limit will only apply to workplace fairness disputes and not other types of employment claims, such as salary-related claims and wrongful dismissal.

sections.label: Private hearings for discrimination claims
sections.summary: All workplace discrimination claims in the ECT or High Court will be heard in private.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Given the inherently sensitive nature of workplace discrimination disputes, all workplace discrimination claims, whether in the ECT or the High Court, will be heard in private.

sections.label: Claim time limits protect reputations
sections.summary: Time limits of one to 12 months protect the reputations of workers and employers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: This protects the reputations of both the workers as well as the employers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: These time limits typically vary from one to 12 months depending on the claimant's circumstances.

sections.label: Striking out frivolous claims
sections.summary: Employers can apply to the judge to strike out frivolous claims.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Employers will be able to apply to the judge for frivolous claims to be struck out.

sections.label: Act implementation targeted end-2027
sections.summary: The Act is targeted for implementation in end-2027, with the timeline adjusted as needed.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: As such, we currently target to implement the Act in end-2027, but we will continue to monitor readiness of all parties and adjust this timeline as necessary.

sections.label: Internal resolution and ECT claims
sections.summary: Parties should resolve disputes internally, then mediate, with adjudication last; ECT handles workplace discrimination claims with increased limits.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: We encourage all parties to resolve their disputes internally, then seek third-party mediation if necessary, with adjudication as the last resort.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: We have also designated the ECT to be the main forum for workplace discrimination disputes and increased the claim limits to allow more workers, including PMEs, to benefit from the ECT.

sections.label: Grievance process, mediation, ECT limits
sections.summary: Employees should use the firm's grievance process then mediation, and ECT limits for workplace discrimination claims are increased with safeguards against frivolous claims.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: An employee should first go through the firm's own grievance handling process, and failing which, both parties should attempt mediation.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: We want to provide more workers with access to a forum that is affordable and that can expeditiously resolves their claims.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: This is why we are increasing the limit at the ECT for workplace discrimination claims.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: We also put in place safeguards to deter and deal with frivolous claims.

sections.label: Model resolves discrimination issues quickly
sections.summary: The designed model enables workplace discrimination issues to be discussed and resolved quickly while ensuring just outcomes.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: The model that we have carefully designed enables workplace discrimination issues to be discussed and to be resolved quickly while ensuring just outcomes.

sections.label: Workplace Fairness Act protection
sections.summary: The Workplace Fairness Act was passed in January to strengthen protection against common forms of discrimination, giving workers individual recourse including compensation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: After a while, they doubted their own value, and this chipped away their confidence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: I am heartened that through NTUC and our tripartite partners' efforts over the many years, the Workplace Fairness Act was passed in January to strengthen protection against the most common forms of discrimination faced by our workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: For the first time, workers who face discrimination – whether in hiring, promotion or dismissal – will be able to obtain individual recourse, including compensation for losses suffered.

sections.label: Employment claims process outcomes
sections.summary: MOM's 2024 Employment Standards Report states over 80% of employment claims were resolved at TADM within two months, with over 90% of claimants fully recovering salaries and payments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: This claims process has worked well for other employment claims, such as salary and wrongful dismissal.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: And according to MOM's 2024 Employment Standards Report, more than 80% of employment claims were resolved at TADM within two months, with more than 90% of claimants fully recovering their salaries and payments at TADM and the ECT.

sections.label: Unions and ECT claims limit
sections.summary: The Bill affirms unions' roles, and the ECT claims limit raised to $250,000 for workplace fairness claims lets unions support and represent more members, including PMEs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: I am glad that the Bill recognises and affirms the vital roles played by our unions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: And with the ECT claims limit being raised to $250,000 for workplace fairness claims, our unions now can support and represent even more members, including more of the PMEs.

sections.label: Flexibility for exceptional discrimination cases
sections.summary: A request that the Government consider more flexibility in exceptional cases, such as workers who did not reasonably know they were discriminated against or lack English language access.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: Could the Government consider a little bit more flexibility in exceptional cases – for example, if a worker did not reasonably know that they were being discriminated against, the ground can be very uneven, and some of our workers may not have access even to the English language, and may face many difficulties in understanding that they have been discriminated against, so it will be appreciated if the Government can consider a little bit of flexibility in such exceptional cases.

sections.label: Union resolution of workplace disputes
sections.summary: About 95% of workplace dispute cases are resolved at the enterprise level with union assistance, and the Bill's amendments let unions help and represent more workers including PMEs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: Approximately 95% of workplace dispute cases are resolved at the enterprise level with union assistance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: With the amendments to this Bill, our unions will be able to help and represent more workers – including Professionals, Managers, and Executives (PMEs) – providing them with a fair and viable avenue for grievances.

sections.label: Progress against workplace discrimination
sections.summary: The speaker states that Singapore has come a long way in strengthening protection against workplace discrimination.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: (In English): Mr Deputy Speaker, Sir, we have come a long way in strengthening protection against workplace discrimination.

sections.label: Claim limits and ECT adjudication
sections.summary: Unsettled cases go to the ECT up to $250,000 or the High Court beyond that, exceeding salary and wrongful dismissal claim limits.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: If a settlement agreement is not reached, the case would be adjudicated at either the ECT for claims up to and inclusive of $250,000, or the High Court for amounts beyond that.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: On a tangential point about the claim limits for cases heard before the ECT, the $250,000 benchmark far exceeds the claim limits for salary and wrongful dismissal claims which are $20,000 and $30,000 respectively, depending on whether one attends union-facilitated mediation.

sections.label: Discrimination victims not seeking help
sections.summary: Many workers with protected characteristics lack resources to pursue claims, and 70.7% of discrimination respondents did not seek help.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Many workers with protected characteristics may not have the resources to engage in proceedings that they are unfamiliar with, to gather extensive documentary evidence or to take time off work to pursue claims, given the significant opportunity costs involved.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: It is shocking, yet telling, that according to the MOM's Fair Employment Practices Report for 2023, 70.7%, a significant majority of respondents who reported having experienced discrimination at work, did not seek help.

sections.label: TADM mediation resolution rate
sections.summary: MOM's 2024 Employment Standards Report suggests over 80% of employment claims reaching TADM are resolved through mediation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: MOM's 2024 Employment Standards Report does suggest its effectiveness in resolving employment disputes, with over 80% of all employment claims that make it to the TADM resolved through mediation.

sections.label: Prima facie evidence for discrimination claims
sections.summary: Recommendation 15 states claimants should provide prima facie evidence such as emails, messages or signed oral testimonies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Recommendation 15 of the Tripartite Committee's report notes that when lodging a workplace discrimination claim, the claimant should provide prima facie evidence such as emails, mobile phone messages or signed oral testimonies to support their case that discrimination has occurred.

sections.label: Publication of selected ECT judgments
sections.summary: From the second half of 2026 the Judiciary would publish selected ECT judgments, with judgments available on request and approval.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In a reply to a Parliamentary Question raised earlier this year by my Sengkang group representation constituency (GRC) colleague Ms He Ting Ru, the Manpower Minister shared that starting from the second half of 2026, the Judiciary would publish selected ECT judgments, while judgments would continue to be made available to individuals upon request and with the Courts' approval.

sections.label: Time bars for employment claims
sections.summary: Time bars are one month for pre-employment, six months for in-employment and one month after employment for end-employment claims.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The limit is one month after the date of notice for pre-employment, six months after the date of notice for in-employment and one month after the last day of employment for end-employment claims.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: However, for pre- and post- employment claims, the claimant would also be busy with the job search process, thus leaving them with very little time, energy or mind space to build their case.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Hence, would the Government clarify how it determined the duration of the time bars and would they consider extending them, especially for pre- and post- employment cases, in the interest of our workers?

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: To round up, Mr Deputy Speaker, in my speech I have sought to emphasise five critical themes: the need to review claim limits for salary and wrongful dismissal alongside the new $250,000 cap for discrimination; ensuring access to the claims process for workers who are already disadvantaged; clarifying the evidential burden and establishing protections against the structural power imbalance that favours employers; strengthening transparency through publication of anonymised judgments and company names; and reconsidering time bars that may otherwise exclude workers still navigating job transitions.

sections.label: Workplace grievances involving pregnancy
sections.summary: Of over 3,000 workplace grievances recorded by the Labour Movement between 2024 and mid-2025, around 40 involved pregnancy, discrimination or harassment.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: Between 2024 and the first half of 2025, of over 3,000 individual workplace grievances recorded by the Labour Movement, around 40 involved pregnancy, discrimination, or harassment.

sections.label: Bill requires grievance handling systems
sections.summary: The Bill requires employers to establish grievance handling systems and protect employees from retaliation when they raise concerns.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: They are common experiences of silence of quiet resignation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: And that is why it is critical that this Bill requires employers to establish proper grievance handling systems and to protect employees from retaliation when they raise concerns.

sections.label: Kelly's maternity benefits case
sections.summary: An employer tried to avoid maternity benefits, unaware part-time employees are entitled after three months of service; the Bill would have allowed Kelly further redress.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: When she sought NTUC's help, we discovered the employer had attempted to avoid maternity benefits, unaware that part-time employees are equally entitled after three months of service.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: Had this Bill been in place, Kelly would have sought further redress for pre-employment discrimination under this law.

sections.label: Strengthening representation ecosystem
sections.summary: The ecosystem of representation must be strengthened for those between jobs, new to the workforce or unaware of help, possibly with a longer time bar.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: For those in between jobs, new to the workforce, or unaware of available help, we must strengthen this ecosystem of representation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: And we might look towards having a longer time bar so that our people would be able to get more advice.

sections.label: Safeguards against unfounded accusations
sections.summary: The Bill's safeguards require credible evidence from formal investigation, encourage early mediation and ensure confidentiality; a 2022 survey found one in three respondents' companies communicated anti-discrimination policies.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: For such employers, an unfounded accusation can cause distress, not just financially, but personally.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: I therefore welcome the safeguards in this Bill requiring credible evidence from formal investigation, encouraging early mediation and ensuring confidentiality in proceedings.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: In a 2022 survey by the NTUC Women and Family team, and the PAP Women's Wing of 3,000 respondents, just one in three shared that their companies have communicated policies against workplace discrimination and these were more likely to be respondents who worked in companies with more than 200 employees.

sections.label: SMEs commit to fair workplaces
sections.summary: Over 2,000 SMEs in the Labour Movement network have committed to providing fair, progressive and safe workplaces.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: Today, over 2,000 SMEs in our Labour Movement network have already committed to providing fair, progressive and safe workplaces.

sections.label: Bill and Workplace Fairness Act
sections.summary: This Bill and the Workplace Fairness Act passed on 8 January 2025 are a significant step forward in protecting Singapore's workers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: Workers feel respected and motivated, and our Singapore society, grows even more cohesive.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This Bill, together with the Workplace Fairness Act passed on 8 January 2025, represents a significant step forward in protecting Singapore's workers.

sections.label: Wrongful dismissal time limit cases
sections.summary: A 2022 reply said about 6% of wrongful dismissal claims filed with TADM each year exceeded the time limit, and asks about settlements and 2024-2025 extension appeals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: According to a Parliamentary reply by Senior Minister of State Dr Koh Poh Koon in 2022, approximately 6% of wrongful dismissal claims filed with TADM each year exceeded the time limit.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: How many of such cases actually achieved settlement, and critically in 2024 and 2025, how many appeals for time extensions were filed and how many were granted?

sections.label: Extending WFA to outsourced workers
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Ministry plans to extend WFA protection to outsourced workers in future amendments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Does the Ministry plan to extend WFA protection to outsourced workers in future amendments?

sections.label: Representation for union members and executives
sections.summary: Currently, union members cannot be represented during discussions, whilst executives have an even more limited representation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Currently, union members cannot be represented during discussions – whilst executives have an even more limited representation.

sections.label: One-month mediation filing deadline
sections.summary: Workers who have been dismissed need to file for mediation within just one month from their last day.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Workers who have been dismissed need to file for mediation within just one month from their last day.

sections.label: WFA coverage of vulnerable workers
sections.summary: The Workplace Fairness Act does not cover contract workers, platform workers, and outsourced workers, and the passage urges a framework to extend protection to outsourced workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The Workplace Fairness Act (WFA) does not cover contract workers, platform workers, and outsourced workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: They are the group that is most vulnerable to discrimination.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I urge that a framework be established to extend protection to outsourced workers.

sections.label: ECT jurisdiction and non-unionised workers
sections.summary: MOM's rationale for raising the ECT monetary jurisdiction to S$250,000 for discrimination claims is acknowledged, but non-unionised workers cannot have legal representation in mediation or ECT proceedings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: First, I acknowledge MOM's rationale for expanding the ECT monetary jurisdiction to S$250,000 for discrimination claims, a positive step for many PMEs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: However, non-unionised workers are disadvantaged due to the inability to have legal representation during mediation or ECT proceedings, especially given the complexity of proving discrimination.

sections.label: High Court publication and platform workers
sections.summary: The Minister is asked whether the High Court's discretion to publish is flexible enough for public accountability of employers found to have committed discriminatory acts, and the Bill excludes 67,600 platform workers recorded in 2024.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Will the Minister confirm that the High Court's discretion to publish is flexible enough to ensure public accountability of employers found to have committed discriminatory acts, even without criminal prosecution, to avoid undermining the deterrence effect of this legislation?

sentences.speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: While the Bill covers about three-quarters of the local workforce, this excludes the 67,600 platform workers recorded in 2024.

sections.label: Employees' right to seek redress
sections.summary: Employees will have a direct right to seek redress on discrimination through a defined process of mediation and, when necessary, adjudication by the ECT or the High Court.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Employees will have a direct right to seek redress on discrimination through a defined process of mediation and when necessary, adjudication by the ECT or the High Court.

sections.label: TADM guidelines on discrimination claims
sections.summary: The Minister is asked whether TADM will publish information and guidelines on filing discrimination claims, similar to those for salary, salary-related, employment or dismissal claims.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Ensuring that help is not only available, but understandable and useable will make the right to redress truly meaningful.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: I would therefore like to ask the Minister: will TADM be publishing information and guidelines on filing discrimination claim, similar to what have been done for salary, salary-related, employment or dismissal claims?

sections.label: Right to bring discrimination claim
sections.summary: The passage asks whether they have a right to bring a claim for discrimination.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Do they have a right to bring a claim for discrimination?

sections.label: Safeguards against frivolous claims
sections.summary: The passage asks what safeguards will identify and dismiss clearly unsubstantiated or frivolous claims early so small employers are not subject to unnecessary administrative or reputational burden.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: What safeguards will be in place to identify and dismiss clearly unsubstantiated or frivolous claims early so that small employers are not subject to unnecessary administrative or even reputational burden?

sections.label: Data sharing under section 45
sections.summary: New section 45 of the Workplace Fairness Bill lets the Commissioner or Registrar share data for policy formulation or public interest.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: The proposed new section 45 of the Workplace Fairness Bill allows the Commissioner or the Registrar of the High Court to share data to the public agency for the purpose of policy formulation or review, or to a public agency as is necessary in the public interest.

sections.label: Possible new heads of damage
sections.summary: The question asks whether there would be other new heads of damage beyond loss of earnings, benefits and expenses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Aside from possible loss of earnings, possible loss of benefits and even possibly expenses arising from discrimination, such as actual medical expenses to treat stress caused by discrimination, for example, which may arguably be supported under current laws on quantum, would there be other new heads of damage?

sections.label: Complaint materials and languages
sections.summary: The Member asks if TADM will publish materials on lodging discrimination complaints and if Government will use multiple languages.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: For them, lodging a complaint is like walking into an unfamiliar place, completely lost and not knowing where to begin.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: So I would like to ask the Minister: First, will the Tripartite Alliance for Dispute Management (TADM) publish appropriate and sufficient materials and guidelines so that workers clearly understand how to lodge complaints about workplace discrimination?

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Second, will the Government use multiple languages – including Chinese, Malay and Tamil – so that more employees also know their rights?

sections.label: Conciliation outcomes in other countries
sections.summary: The passage cites UK, Australian and New Zealand figures on discrimination cases resolved through conciliation, mediation or early resolution.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In the UK, over 70% of early conciliation cases via the Advisory, Conciliation and Arbitration Service are resolved without going to tribunal, usually within four to six weeks.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Australia's Fair Work Commission resolves around 60% to 70% of discrimination cases at conciliation; quick, informal, inexpensive.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In New Zealand, the Human Rights Commission closes 94% of discrimination complaints through mediation or early resolution, with 77% satisfaction.

sections.label: Burden of proof for retaliation
sections.summary: In the UK and Australia, the burden of proof for retaliatory action shifts to the employer once a prima facie case is established.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In jurisdictions like the UK and Australia, the burden of proof for retaliatory action shifts to the employer once the employee has established a prima facie case.

sections.label: Review of protected characteristics
sections.summary: The Member hopes MOM will commit to a phased review of protected characteristics guided by mediation data and tripartite feedback.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Neurodivergent employees, platform and freelance workers – they form a growing part of our workforce, yet many may not feel fully included, even though TAFEP guidelines apply.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Fairness that feels selective is fairness that can breed resentment.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: So, I hope that MOM will commit to a phased review of protected characteristics in good time, guided by data from mediation cases and tripartite feedback.

sections.label: TAFEP and MOM training role
sections.summary: TAFEP and MOM can train HR managers, supervisors and team leaders.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: TAFEP and MOM can play a key role here, by training not just HR managers, but supervisors and team leaders.

sections.label: Bill strengthens societal compact
sections.summary: The Bill settles disputes and says workers will be judged by contribution, not origin.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In closing, Mr Deputy Speaker, this Bill does not just settle disputes; it strengthens our compact as a society.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: It says to every worker, you will be judged by what you contribute, not by where you come from.

sections.label: Specialised office for workers
sections.summary: The Minister is asked to consider a specialised office giving legal information and advice to aggrieved workers filing claims.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Will the Minister consider setting up a specialised office to provide legal information and advice to aggrieved workers who require assistance in filing their claims?

sections.label: Support persons in proceedings
sections.summary: The Minister is asked to confirm whether employees may have support persons accompany them in proceedings.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Can the Minister confirm if employees will be entitled to have support persons accompanying them in these proceedings?

sections.label: Joint claims and mediation exception
sections.summary: The Minister is asked to consider hearing Workplace Fairness Act and Protection from Harassment Act claims together before the ECT, and giving the commissioner discretion to except serious cases from mandatory mediation.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Would the Minister consider allowing a worker who has experienced both workplace discrimination and workplace harassment to have both their claims under the Workplace Fairness Act and the Protection from Harassment Act heard before the ECT?

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Instead, the commissioner should be given the discretion to make an exception from the mandatory mediation requirement in serious cases where a worker is able to obtain supporting evidence that participation in the mediation will put their mental emotional well-being at risk.

sections.label: Fast dispute resolution timelines
sections.summary: Dispute resolution timelines should be as fast as administratively possible, with clear guidance, so recourse processes do not create barriers or harm.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Third, the timelines for the dispute resolution mechanism should be fast as administratively possible to minimise workers having to deal with the uncertainty and anxiety that come with such legal proceedings.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In particular, it will be helpful to provide claimants and employers with clear guidance on the expected timelines.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The guidance can also help the Ministry to evaluate whether more resources and manpower need to be dedicated to the dispute resolution mechanisms so that claims can be processed and resolved in accordance with target timelines.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: To eradicate workplace discrimination, we must ensure that the processes for workers to seek recourse do not themselves create barriers or cause further harm to the workers who have decided to stand up for themselves.

sections.label: Reservations on excluding smaller firms
sections.summary: The speaker has strong reservations about leaving out firms with fewer than 25 employees from the start.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Next, Mr Deputy Speaker, I have strong reservations about leaving out smaller firms with fewer than 25 employees from the very start.

sections.label: Smaller firms and employee vulnerability
sections.summary: The speaker argues smaller firms' lack of compliance competencies makes their employees more vulnerable, and MOM should help them comply rather than exclude them.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: In fact, I would argue that it is precisely because the smaller firms lack the competencies to comply with this law that makes their employees more vulnerable to workplace discrimination.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: To exclude their employees from the coverage of the WFA is to do them a great disservice.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: I suggest that MOM should actually devote more resources to assist these smaller firms with the process of compliance instead of taking the path of least resistance.

sections.label: Union view of non-unionised employees
sections.summary: From the unions' perspective, the speaker presumes employees of non-unionised companies are more vulnerable, citing PMETs' workforce and union membership shares.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: If I were to use the perspective of the unions, I would naturally presume that employees of non-unionised companies are actually more vulnerable.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: I am thinking of the PMETs in particular, who make up around 63% of our workforce, but their rate of union membership is a lot less, making up about 45% of union members.

sections.label: Clarify ECT union representation segregation
sections.summary: The speaker asks the Minister and union leaders to clarify why union representation at the ECT cannot extend to union members at non-unionised companies.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Will the Minister and/or the union leaders in the House please clarify the reasons for this segregation; why union representation at the ECT cannot be extended to union members at non-unionised companies?

sections.label: Quality of mediators and ECT judges
sections.summary: The speaker says the quality and training of mediators and ECT judges are critical for the system to be seen as fair and just.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: For the system to be perceived as fair and just, and for all parties to have confidence in this process, the quality and training of mediators and, by extension, the quality of ECT judges at the ECT will be absolutely critical.

sections.label: Workplace Fairness Bills on discrimination
sections.summary: The two Workplace Fairness Bills make clear discrimination has no place in workplaces and provide clear consequences where it occurs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: The two Workplace Fairness Bills make it clear that discrimination has no place in our workplaces, and they provide clear consequences where it occurs.

sections.label: Workplace disputes and social compact
sections.summary: The speaker, advisor to two unions representing over 50,000 workers, focuses on the dispute resolution mechanism, sharing employer, worker and social compact perspectives.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: And thankfully, we do not have much experience with workplace disputes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: I am also the advisor to the Singapore Teachers' Union and the Education Services Union, which collectively represent more than 50,000 workers, who mould the future of our nation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The principles of the broader workplace fairness legislation have been debated earlier this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: I will focus only on the dispute resolution mechanism, which is under discussion today.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Specifically, I will share some thoughts from the perspectives of the employer first, and then the worker, and then our overall social compact.

sections.label: Discrimination help-seeking rates
sections.summary: MOM's 2023 Fair Employment Practices Report found about 30% of employees who experienced discrimination sought help, down from 35% the year before.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: MOM's Fair Employment Practices Report in 2023 found that only about 30% of employees who experienced discrimination sought help, a decrease from 35% of the year before.

sections.label: Judge-led ECT and claim limits
sections.summary: The judge-led ECT model needs no lawyers, and the expanded claim limit of up to $250,000 lets more PMEs seek accessible justice, with MOM able to pursue state enforcement action.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The judge-led ECT model, without the need for lawyers, levels the playing field for workers, including those who are PMEs, and the expanded claim limit of up to $250,000 means more PMEs can seek accessible and affordable justice.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: For serious breaches, especially those that undermine our shared values of race and religion, I note that MOM can also pursue state enforcement action against employers where public intent requires it.

sections.label: Calibrating naming and sanctioning employers
sections.summary: The passage asks how MOM will calibrate when to exercise discretion to name and sanction employers while preserving fairness and confidentiality for individuals involved.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: How will MOM calibrate when to exercise discretion to name and sanction employers, while still preserving fairness and confidentiality for individuals involved?

sections.label: Guidance for smaller companies
sections.summary: MOM and TAFEP will continue to guide employers, especially SMEs with limited HR capabilities, in setting fair, simple and confidential grievance channels.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: This is especially important for smaller companies, where a timely conversation, a listening ear, or a fair explanation can prevent tension from mounting and turning into a claim.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: I am encouraged that MOM and TAFEP will continue to guide employers in setting a fair, simple and confidential grievance channels, especially for SMEs with limited HR capabilities.

sections.label: Unions, MOM and employers partnership
sections.summary: Unions working with MOM and employers help make fairness felt, not feared, and the Bill reflects this partnership, assuring workers of fair redress and employers of clear processes.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Our unions, working alongside MOM and employers, help to make fairness felt, not feared, guiding workers and companies through challenges with calm, respect and trust.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: This Bill reflects that partnership in action: workers assured of fair redress, employers confident of clear processes and a society strengthened by mutual respect.

sections.label: Fairness, dignity and mutual respect
sections.summary: The law ensures every worker is treated fairly and with compassion regardless of race, religion, age, gender, disability or mental health condition.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: But fairness is not merely about laws, it is about dignity, humanity and mutual respect for one another.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: This law ensures that every worker, regardless of race, religion, age, gender, or those with disabilities or mental health condition, are treated fairly and with compassion.

sections.label: Respected workers build united Singapore
sections.summary: When every worker feels respected and valued, stronger workplaces and a stronger, more united Singapore are built.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: When every worker, regardless of race, religion, or background, feels respected and valued, we build not just stronger workplaces, but a stronger, more united Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: This is a landmark Bill: fair, forward-looking and rooted in trust.

sections.label: Workplace Fairness Bill 2025 shield
sections.summary: The Workplace Fairness Bill 2025 provides a more robust shield against discrimination than what previously existed.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Speaker, Sir, the Workplace Fairness Bill 2025 provides a more robust shield against discrimination than what previously existed.

sections.label: Legal representation and union members
sections.summary: Legal representation is not allowed, and only union members can be represented by their unions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Legal representation, already often costly, is not allowed, and only union members can be represented by their unions.

sections.label: Independent advocate for vulnerable workers
sections.summary: The right for vulnerable workers to have a trained, independent advocate present during all proceedings should be legally entrenched.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: To achieve this, we should legally entrench the right for vulnerable workers to have a trained, independent advocate present during all proceedings – from internal meetings and mediations to hearings throughout the resolution process.

sections.label: Legislate reasonable accommodation duty
sections.summary: SG Enable and the Enabling Employment Credit have supported employers to hire persons with disabilities, and it is time to legislate the duty to provide reasonable accommodation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: SG Enable and the Enabling Employment Credit have done extensive work to educate and support employers to hire persons with disabilities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: It is now time to take the next step – to legislate the duty to provide reasonable accommodation.

sections.label: Codifying reasonable accommodation duty
sections.summary: The passage calls for codifying into law the employer's positive duty to provide reasonable accommodation, with failure being discrimination.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: There are many, many more examples – across both blue, white new collar jobs, silver jobs – documented by the various organisations such as SG Enable and their Job Placement and Job Support agencies, partners such as SPD, ARC and MINDS.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: It is timely, therefore, to explicitly codify into law the employer's positive duty to provide reasonable accommodation – and to recognise that failure to do so is an act of discrimination.

sections.label: Workplace Fairness Audits for employers
sections.summary: The passage asks all medium and large employers to carry out regular Workplace Fairness Audits to stop discrimination before it happens.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: A fair system should stop discrimination before it happens – not fix it after people are hurt.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: We should ask all medium and large employers to carry out regular Workplace Fairness Audits.

sections.label: Consolidating dispute resolution pathway
sections.summary: The passage states that consolidating dispute resolution into a single statutory pathway aims to provide clarity and accessibility.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: By consolidating dispute resolution into a single, statutory pathway, it aims to provide clarity and accessibility.

sections.label: Support for the Bill
sections.summary: The passage states support for the Bill while looking forward to MOM's consideration of four proposals.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Notwithstanding this and looking forward to MOM's consideration of my four proposals, I support the Bill.
